newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Philips in talks to cut Grundig stake.
newsitem.headline: Philips in talks to cut Grundig stake.

text.p: Philips Electronics NV said on Thursday it was talking to "financial investors" with a view to cutting its 31.6 percent stake in loss making German audio-visual equipment maker Grundig .
"We're talking to financial investors, only financial investors," said Philips spokesman Ben Geerts. "We do not wish to mention any names before anything has been concluded," he added.

Geerts was responding to questions after a report in the Frankfurter Allgemeine Zeitung that Philips might sell its stake in Grundig to small London merchant bank Botts & Co for a possible private placement.

"What I told the Frankfurter is that we have said earlier that we are investigating possibilities to reduce our stake in Grundig and that we are investigating possibilities to find financial investors," Geerts told Reuters.
Geerts declined to comment on whether the talks centred on selling all of Philips' stake in Grundig or only part of it.
"We cannot be more specific at the moment," he said.

Philips is still in talks with the Grundig family and the Max Grundig Foundation about disentangling its links with Grundig, which last month reported a 631 million mark ($360 million) loss in 1996, compared to a 598 million mark loss the year before.
Geerts said Grundig currently held an option to sell 52 percent of the company to Philips, back from 68 percent after a recent deal with a German investor.
Geerts said Philips was still talking to the Grundig Foundation about disentangling itself from the option and its commitment to pay a 46 million mark a year dividend to the Grundig family heirs.
Philips under the chairmanship of Cor Boonstra has taken a rigorous approach to Grundig, which has been in loss for years.

In January, just two months after Boonstra took up the reins at Philips, the Dutch company said it would no longer automatically reimburse Grundig its losses. Instead it would account for Grundig's losses on a pro-rata basis related to its 31.6 pct stake and take a "passive minority" stance to Grundig.
